From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up

Thanks again for the call today – great to meet you, Lisa. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can put together a targeted capacity and pricing estimate for Acme.

Recap of your stated needs:
- Deployment mode: leaning toward Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) for predictable latency and data isolation.
- Primary use: customer-facing chat + retrieval-augmented responses.
- Timeline: procurement and POC in Q4, production early Q1.

Open items we discussed (can you confirm these?):
1) TPS and concurrency targets (sustained vs peak).
2) Average prompt vs completion token mix (avg prompt tokens / avg response tokens).
3) Model(s) you anticipate using (e.g., Llama 3 chat 70B, mix of 13B for lower-cost routes).
4) Any strict latency SLOs (p95 target) and region/data residency constraints.

Next steps: if you can reply with TPS (sustained + peak), concurrency, and token averages we will run a quick sizing exercise. Attached is a rough capacity worksheet and a one-page SOW stub to accelerate procurement.

Looking forward – I’ll loop in Rafael (solutions) and Aditya (dedicated infra) to run sizing once we have numbers.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa – appreciate the recap. Confirming numbers from our side:
- Sustained TPS: ~30 transactions/sec (chat requests)
- Peak TPS: up to ~150 TPS during batch notification windows (short bursts, ~10-15 minutes)
- Expected concurrent active sessions: ~50 (users holding live chats)
- Token mix: avg user prompt ~80 tokens, avg model response ~300 tokens
- Models: primary is a 70B chat-style model (we're evaluating Llama-3-chat-70B), with a portion of traffic (roughly 30%) falling back to a 13B model for cheaper queries
- Preferred GPU: we'd prefer H100s if that materially improves latency; open to recommendations on A100 if cost tradeoffs make sense
- Data residency: US only; SOC2/ISO evidence required for procurement review

Procurement contact is cc'd (procurement@acme.ai) – they will need the SOW and an initial pricing sheet to start terms review. Can you also include a rough timeline for POC -> production and an early ballpark for monthly committed spend for the Dedicated pool?

Thanks,
Lisa
Head of Product Engineering | Acme AI
lisa.chen@acme.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Hi Lisa – great, this is exactly what we need to run a sizing pass. A few quick notes while Rafael and Aditya pull the detailed numbers:
- We'll size for your peak burst (150 TPS) with steady-state autoscaling down to sustain ~30 TPS. That keeps costs predictable while handling spikes.
- H100 is a solid pick for low-latency 70B chat – it will reduce GPU count vs A100 but at a higher unit cost. Rafael will provide the comparative GPU counts and a recommended baseline.
- For mixed workloads we typically propose a small pool of high-performance GPUs (for the 70B chat path) plus a separate pool or on-demand instances for the 13B fallback to improve unit economics.

I attached the capacity-estimate-acme.xlsx (worksheet has slots for token mix/latency targets) and the SOW stub procurement asked for.

Proposed next steps:
1) Rafael to share a baseline GPU count and rough cost delta (H100 vs A100).
2) Schedule a 30-min sizing call with your infra/eng + procurement this week to align on timeline and contractual items.
3) I’ll follow up with a preliminary committed-cost estimate for Redwood Dedicated based on the baseline.

Thanks again – looping Rafael and Aditya in.

Best,
Marissa

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 07 Nov 2026 10:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up

Marissa / Aditya – ran a quick back-of-envelope based on Lisa's numbers (70B chat primary, 30% 13B fallback, avg tokens 80/300, peak 150 TPS, concurrency ~50):

High-level recommendations:
- GPU choice: H100 (80GB) for the 70B chat instances gives the best latency and reduces total GPU count; A100 (80GB) is viable but will need ~35-50% more GPUs for the same p95.
- Baseline sizing (to support 150 TPS peak with ~200-400ms p95 for chat generation):
  - H100 path: ~8 H100 GPUs (quantized 4-bit, optimized kernels, batching) as a starting point; supports autoscale down to ~3 GPUs for steady state (30 TPS).
  - A100 path: ~12 A100 GPUs for comparable latency.
- 13B fallback: can be served from a separate smaller pool (2-3 A100/H100 or dedicated shared instances) – significantly cheaper per token.
- Concurrency & batching: plan for ~50 concurrency with dynamic batching (max batch size tuned to meet latency p95). Prefix caching for repeated context can reduce compute needs for similar requests.

Caveats & items to validate on call:
- Exact model variant (quantization + kernel support) – if you pick a variant we don't have optimized kernels for, perf changes.
- Allowed latency p95 (I used a target ~200-400ms; confirm if stricter).
- Bursting cadence – sustained 150 TPS for 10-15 minutes vs many short spikes changes autoscaling strategy.

Action items:
- Marissa: schedule sizing call with Acme infra + procurement (30 min).
- Aditya: run a quick perf sim with our internal runner for the 70B quantized path and share numbers (tokens/sec per GPU) so we can refine the GPU count.
- I’ll draft an H100 vs A100 comparison sheet with estimated monthly committed cost ranges for 8 vs 12 GPUs and include the mixed-pool option.

Rafael Mendes
Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com
